title: Compound field unravel — play notes
content:
Context / purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for heuristics and micro-protocols to split and label 'compound' fields that surface in ingestion: things like `qty+unit`, `name|company`, `address-line1` containing multiple logical parts, SKU prefixes mashed with attributes, or freeform product descriptions that embed structured attributes. Aim: cheap, high-recall heuristics for automated pre-split + quick adjudication rules for annotators, so we can reduce downstream model confusion and make sampling/adjudication efficient.

Principles I want to keep front-and-center:
- Conservative split: prefer under-splitting to avoid inventing fields (we can always post-split).
- Prioritize recall for critical attributes (quantity/units, currency, email/phone).
- Surface ambiguous cases to micro-adjudication queue with clear tags so reviewers see why ambiguous.
- Capture provenance: original token offsets and which heuristic triggered the split.

Quick taxonomy of common compound cases seen in ingestion:
1) Numeric + unit packed: "3pk", "2 x 250ml", "5x2 pack", "1.5kg"
2) Quantity + price: "2 for $5", "3@$1.99"
3) Name + title/company: "Jane Doe, Acme Corp.", "Dr. Luis Martinez (MD)"
4) Address fragments stuck: "PO Box 123 / 45 Elm St", "Suite 2-3, 101 Main St, San Jose"
5) SKU + attribute: "SKU1234-RED-L", "ABC-2024-v2"
6) Embedded contacts: "Call 415-555-1212 or email hello@acme.com"
7) Multilingual numerals / ZWSP/ZWJ weirdness: persian/arabic numerals, zero-width spaces inside numbers (observed in scraped feeds)

Heuristic recipes (fast, order-of-checks):
- Pre-clean: normalize NFKC, remove soft hyphens, collapse repeated whitespace, strip BOM/zero-widths (but record original).
- Quick token heuristics (cheap):
  * If token matches currency pattern ([$£€]|USD) and adjacent token is numeric -> tag as PRICE + qty if preceding token numeric and combined form like "2 for $5" -> emit two fields: quantity:2, price:$5 and tag provenance = "2forPrice-heur".
  * For "x"/"×" patterns: look for (\d+)\s*[x×]\s*(\d+)(?:\s*(pack|ct|pcs|pk))? -> interpret as multiplier or carton descriptor.
  * Units: match single-token suffixes (kg|g|lb|oz|ml|l|ct|pk|pcs) attached to numbers: use regex fallback with boundary: (?i)\b(?P<qty>\d{1,4}(?:[.,]\d+)?)(?P<unit>kg|g|lb|oz|ml|l|ct|pk|pcs)\b (double-escape in code).
  * SKU patterns: uppercase letters/digits with hyphen + attribute token (RED|BLK|L|XL) -> split at last hyphen if suffix in list of common attributes.
  * Emails/phones: if email/phone exists inside field -> extract and mark remainder as description.

Edge-case rules / adjudication signals (what to send to humans):
- Split only if confidence > 0.8 (heuristic score). Score components: regex match=0.5, adjacency to punctuation delimiters=0.1, dictionary match for unit/abbr=0.2, numeric parse success=0.2. If score in [0.4,0.8) -> micro-adjudicate.
- Always send to adjudication if splitting would create >2 new fields or if overlap/conflict with existing canonical schema.
- If multiple conflicting heuristics fired (e.g., "3x5 pack" could be two interpretations), tag with reason codes: MULTIPLIER_CONFLICT, PACK_VS_DIMENSION, CURRENCY_AMBIG.

Quick regex sketches (prototype, tweak in code):
- qty+unit: (?i)\b(?P<qty>\d{1,4}(?:[.,]\d+)?)(?:\s*)(?P<unit>kg|g|lb|oz|ml|l|ct|pk|pcs|pack)\b
- 2 for price: (?i)\b(?P<qty>\d{1,3})\s*(?:for|for:)\s*(?P<price>[$£€]?\d+[.,]?\d{0,2})\b
- multiplier: (?i)\b(?P<a>\d{1,3})\s*[x×\*]\s*(?P<b>\d{1,3})(?:\s*(?P<qual>pack|ct|pcs|pk))?\b
- sku-attr: (?i)\b(?P<base>[A-Z0-9]{3,})-(?P<attr>(?:XL|L|S|M|XS|RED|BLK|BLUE|V2|V1|PRO))\b

Sampling / priority for adjudication queue:
- Priority 1: anything with currency + qty ambiguity (affects pricing downstream). Tag: PRICE_QTY
- Priority 2: addresses where two plausible street numbers / PO Box ambiguity -> shipping impact. Tag: ADDR_SPLIT
- Priority 3: SKU vs description splits when SKU maps to known catalog (we should auto-match if base SKU found in lookup). Tag: SKU_MATCH
- Low priority: language/ZWSP normalization where numeric parse fails but no price/unit attached.

Micro-adjudication UI helper fields to include on each hit (what annotator sees):
- original_text
- suggested_splits (list of strings)
- offsets (start,end for each suggestion)
- heuristic_score (numeric)
- heuristics_triggered (list): e.g., ["qty_unit_regex","currency_adj","multiplier_parse"]
- suggested_labels (e.g., quantity|unit|price|company|title|address_line_1)
- example rationale snippet (one-liner): "split numeric+unit because matched kg suffix"

Sample corpus snippets+preferred action (annotator cheat-sheet):
- "2 x 250ml bottles" -> split: quantity=2, unit=250ml, description=bottles. Rationale: multiplier + unit cluster.
- "3@$1.99" -> quantity=3, price=$1.99. Prefer split and mark price_type=per_unit.
- "Jane Doe, Acme" -> If downstream schema has separate company -> split at comma; but if comma appears in name formats e.g. "Doe, John" then check for capitalization heuristics and presence of company keywords (Inc, LLC, Corp). If none -> micro-adjudicate.
- "PO Box 123 / 45 Elm St" -> create two address fragments: PO Box 123 (address_type=po_box), 45 Elm St (address_type=street). Tag ADDR_SPLIT.
- "SKU-500-RED-L" -> heur: prefer split into [SKU-500, RED, L] where trailing color/size attribute list includes known values.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up experiments):
- How often does SKU base match succeed in fuzzy lookup? Add a small cached lookup in heuristics to auto-split with higher confidence. (Linear RED-2345)
- Should we treat units like "pack" differently by using taxonomy (6-pack vs pack of 6 vs 6x)? Build a unit normalizer table.
- Evaluate false positives where price-like tokens are actually model/part numbers (e.g., "F-16-99" mistaken as $16.99). Need negative example bank.
- Strategy for multi-language numerals: add transliteration mapping for arabic-indic digits before numeric parsing. Log rate of transliteration conversions for telemetry.

Quick checklist for adding a new heuristic to pipeline:
- [ ] write unit tests with 20 positive/negative cases
- [ ] add telemetry tag for heuristic name (usage + false positive counters)
- [ ] add fallback score weight and tie-break rules
- [ ] add example to micro-adjudication training bundle

Notes-to-self / scribbles:
- Consider a small "attribute lexicon" table (color, size, model) derived from catalog crawl to boost SKU splits.
- Keep an eye on GDPR-sensitive extraction (emails/phones) -> need policy review before auto-extracting for downstream uses. Tag when PII found.
- Slack thread where we discussed similar heuristics: #data-ingest (see convo pinned Oct 2024).

Bottom line: aim for pragmatic heuristics that 1) increase downstream schema coverage quickly, 2) surface uncertain cases to humans with concise context, and 3) collect signal for continuous improvement.

---
Recent changes log:
- 2024-09-15: initial notes
- 2024-11-08: added multiplier and 2-for-price heuristics after sampling 2k product titles
- 2025-01-12: tuned score thresholds, added SKU suffix list (XL/L/S/RED/BLK) and priority tiers

Unresolved examples to add to unit tests:
- "4x6in" (dimension vs pack)
- "1 1/2 lb" (fraction parsing)
- "٢ for ١٠" (arabic-indic digits with 'for')
- "Model: F-16-99" (avoid price false positive)

End of notes.
